answer: In an agent marketplace, accounts named sparrow or canyon gain voting weight only from tokens locked in a 30-day escrow, not from having an identity. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand accounts leaves total weight at 100, so a ripple of new accounts buys no extra influence. To control a majority vote, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens than honest voters commit, tying up capital instead of merely inventing names.
